dinemetric.title: Dinemetric
dinemetric.description: An AI-powered restaurant platform with menu recommendations and insights to support daily operations.
dinemetric.problem: Restaurants often have customer, menu, and operational data spread across different sources, making it difficult to turn that information into useful insights and actionable recommendations.
dinemetric.decision:
The application uses a modern full-stack architecture with Next.js and TypeScript for the frontend and application layer, Supabase for authentication and database functionality, and API integrations for AI-powered features.

Separating the application into reusable UI, data-access, and backend workflows helped keep features maintainable while supporting continued product development.
dinemetric.contribution:
Contributed to the development of Dinemetric, an AI-powered restaurant analytics platform built with Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, and modern full-stack technologies.

My work included developing and improving application features, integrating frontend components with backend services and database workflows, debugging full-stack issues, and supporting AI-powered functionality that transforms restaurant data into structured insights and recommendations.

I also worked with API-driven workflows and application state to ensure data could move reliably between the user interface, backend services, database, and AI features.
dinemetric.outcome: The platform provides restaurant teams with a centralized way to work with business data and AI-generated insights, helping turn complex information into more understandable and actionable recommendations.

smilysis.title: Smilysis
smilysis.description: An application for tracking dental habits and progress with AI-powered scans and personalized insights.
smilysis.problem: Dental issues can develop between regular dental visits, while people often have limited ways to monitor changes in their oral health or understand how daily habits and diet may affect their teeth and gums.
smilysis.decision:
The application combines structured user data with AI-assisted dental-image analysis and health-tracking workflows.

The platform was designed to keep image analysis, oral-care tracking, health insights, and user records within a unified experience, making it easier for users to monitor changes over time rather than relying only on occasional dental visits.
smilysis.contribution:
Contributed to the development of Smilysis, an AI-powered preventive oral-health platform that helps users monitor their dental health between appointments.

I worked on full-stack application features supporting user interactions, dental-health data, and AI-powered workflows. The platform allows users to submit dental images, track oral-care habits, review health-related insights, and receive personalized guidance based on their information.

My work included developing and improving frontend functionality, integrating application workflows with backend services and data storage, and troubleshooting issues across the application stack.
smilysis.outcome: Smilysis provides users with a centralized way to monitor oral-health habits, review AI-assisted dental insights, track changes over time, and better understand factors that may affect their dental health.

sips.title: Sips Cafe
sips.description: A bubble tea ordering platform with menu browsing, payments, and administration tools.
sips.problem: Sips Cafe needed a web-based ordering system that could manage menu items, customization options, customer accounts, orders, and online payments within a single application.
sips.decision:
I designed the application around relational entities representing menu items, orders, customization options, users, and transactions.

Separating these concerns through ASP.NET Core MVC, Entity Framework Core, and structured database relationships made it easier to manage complex order customization while maintaining data consistency.
sips.contribution:
Designed and developed a full-stack cafe ordering application using ASP.NET Core MVC, C#, Entity Framework Core, and a relational database.

I implemented user authentication and authorization, email verification, reCAPTCHA protection, menu and product management, customizable drink options, shopping-cart functionality, and order processing.

I also designed REST-based application workflows, created relational data models for products, orders, transactions, and customization options, and integrated PayPal Checkout for online payments.

Administrative functionality was added to support role-based access and management of menu items and application data.
sips.outcome: The completed application supports the full customer ordering workflow—from account creation and customized product selection through checkout and payment—while also providing administrative functionality for managing menu data and orders.

leadengine.title: LeadEngine
leadengine.description: A lead management platform that automates agent assignment using priority, workload, and capacity rules.
leadengine.problem: Sales teams need a reliable way to distribute incoming leads among agents while considering factors such as agent type, priority, workload, and capacity. Manual assignment can be inconsistent and difficult to scale as the number of leads and agents grows.
leadengine.contribution:
Built a full-stack lead management application using Next.js on the frontend and Django REST Framework on the backend.

I developed agent, manager, and lead management features, including create, edit, detail, search, sorting, and pagination workflows. I also implemented authenticated API communication between the frontend and backend using token-based authentication.

On the backend, I designed REST APIs and database models for agents, managers, and leads, and developed a custom lead-assignment workflow that automatically selects an eligible agent based on agent type, priority, recent lead count, and capacity.

I also built dashboard functionality for visualizing lead and agent data, implemented date-based filtering, and contributed to integration and testing across the application.
leadengine.decision:
I separated the application into a Next.js frontend and Django REST API backend so that the user interface, business logic, and data layer could evolve independently.

The lead-assignment logic was implemented on the backend to keep the business rules centralized and consistent. Agents are evaluated by priority and recent workload, allowing the system to assign leads only to agents who still have available capacity.

I also used PostgreSQL for persistent data storage and API-based communication between the frontend and backend.
leadengine.outcome:
LeadEngine automates lead distribution while giving users a central interface for managing agents, managers, and incoming leads.

The application reduces the need for manual lead assignment and provides a structured way to enforce capacity and priority rules while monitoring lead activity through dashboards and filtered reporting.
